deviation: No Flow | Air to cathode
causes: LCV-200 fails closed or air compressor trips
consequences: No O2/CO2 reaches the cathode. Cell voltage collapses and the cells can reverse. Air no longer cools the stack, so local hot spots form. Fuel keeps flowing to the anode with no reaction, which creates a pressure imbalance between anode and cathode. This can break the wet seal, letting H2 cross over into the cathode and burn inside the stack, damaging it severely. Propulsion power is lost.
safeguards: FIT-110 / FI-110 air flow indication; PIT-110 / PI-110 air pressure indication; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; BPCS control via SIC-400 of LCV-100/200/300
recommendations: Add an independent low-low air flow trip (SIL 1) that closes LCV-100 and LCV-300 and isolates the DC load; Verify LCV-200 fail-safe position and add valve position feedback

deviation: Less Flow | Air to cathode
causes: Air compressor degradation, fouled air intake filter, or SIC-400 / LCV-200 control fault
consequences: The cathode is starved of O2/CO2 and the air does less cooling. Cell voltage drops and stack temperature rises. Local overheating speeds up electrolyte loss and corrosion, and stack life is shortened.
safeguards: FIT-110 / FI-110 air flow indication; TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring; TE-310 / TI-310 cathode outlet temperature; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm
recommendations: Add low air flow alarm on FIT-110 with automatic load reduction; Add a high stack temperature trip independent of the BPCS

deviation: More Flow | Air to cathode
causes: LCV-200 fails open or SIC-400 control fault
consequences: The stack is over-cooled and its temperature falls toward the carbonate freezing point. The electrolyte cracks and gas crosses over. Cathode pressure rises compared with the anode, so the differential across the wet seal goes up. Stack damage is possible.
safeguards: FIT-110 / FI-110 air flow indication; PIT-110 air pressure indication; TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Add high air flow alarm and low stack temperature alarm/trip; Install anode-cathode differential pressure transmitter with alarm

deviation: No Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
causes: LCV-100 fails closed, natural gas compressor trip or water pump trip
consequences: The anode is starved of fuel while current is still being drawn. Cells reverse and the Ni anode oxidises, causing irreversible stack damage. Propulsion power is lost.
safeguards: FIT-100 / FI-100 feed flow indication; PIT-100 feed pressure indication; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; IE-300 / II-300 current monitoring
recommendations: Add a low-low fuel flow / low cell voltage trip that disconnects the DC load; Provide automatic switchover to H2 BOG fuel within permitted load limits

deviation: More Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
causes: LCV-100 fails open or SIC-400 control fault
consequences: Excess endothermic reforming over-cools the stack and creates thermal gradients that can crack the cells. Anode pressure rises. Unreacted fuel is carried to the anode outlet, which can overheat downstream combustion equipment.
safeguards: FIT-100 / FI-100 feed flow indication; TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring; TE-300 / TI-300 anode outlet temperature
recommendations: Add high feed flow alarm on FIT-100 and fuel-to-current ratio limiting in the BPCS

deviation: Other than Composition | Feed (low steam-to-carbon ratio)
causes: Water pump failure or wrong water/natural gas proportion in the feed
consequences: Carbon deposits in the internal reformer and the anode. The catalyst deactivates and flow passages block, causing pressure rise and maldistribution. Stack damage and loss of power follow.
safeguards: FIT-100 total feed flow indication; PIT-100 feed pressure indication
recommendations: Install separate water and natural gas flow measurement with steam-to-carbon ratio control and a low-ratio trip

deviation: As well as Composition | Feed (sulphur / impurities)
causes: Desulphurisation upstream fails or the natural gas supply is off-specification
consequences: The reformer catalyst and Ni anode are poisoned. Performance degrades and stack life is shortened (economic loss).
safeguards: VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm
recommendations: Provide a sulphur analyser downstream of the desulphuriser with alarm

deviation: More Flow | H2 BOG to anode
causes: LCV-300 fails open or a BOG surge from the cargo tanks (ship motion, heat ingress)
consequences: H2 replaces reformate, so less endothermic reforming takes place and the heat balance is lost. The stack overheats and anode pressure rises. Electrolyte loss, seal damage and possible H2 leakage follow.
safeguards: FIT-120 / FI-120 H2 flow indication; PIT-120 H2 pressure indication; TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Add high H2 flow alarm and a high-high stack temperature trip that closes LCV-300; Limit the H2 BOG share of fuel in the BPCS with feed-forward on FIT-120

deviation: No Flow | H2 BOG to anode
causes: LCV-300 fails closed or H2 BOG compressor trip
consequences: Fuel to the anode drops and power output falls. If the load is not reduced, the anode is starved locally. BOG builds up in the cargo tanks (outside this node).
safeguards: FIT-120 / FI-120 H2 flow indication; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; BPCS fuel flow control via SIC-400
recommendations: Implement automatic compensation by feed flow (LCV-100) and load reduction on low H2 flow

deviation: More Pressure | Stack anode / cathode
causes: BV-400 or BV-410 (fail-closed) closes spuriously or loses its signal/actuating air while the inlets remain open
consequences: The outlet is blocked and pressure in the stack rises. The wet seals fail and hot H2/CO-rich gas is released into the machinery space. Fire or explosion and CO toxicity can cause multiple fatalities.
safeguards: PSV-160 to Vent Out; BV-160 (fail-open) vent valve; PIT-100 / PIT-110 / PIT-120 inlet pressure indication
recommendations: Install stack pressure transmitters on anode and cathode with an independent high-high pressure SIF (SIL 2) that closes LCV-100/200/300 and opens BV-160; Add position feedback on BV-400 and BV-410, interlocked with the inlet valves; Verify PSV-160 sizing for the blocked-outlet case and that it protects both anode and cathode

deviation: More Pressure | Anode-to-cathode differential
causes: Mismatch between fuel (LCV-100/LCV-300) and air (LCV-200) flows, or uneven throttling of BV-400 against BV-410
consequences: The electrolyte wet seal is broken and gas crosses over. H2/CO burns directly with air inside the stack, causing hot spots and cell or stack destruction. A fire may spread outside the stack.
safeguards: PIT-100 / PIT-110 / PIT-120 inlet pressure indication; TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm
recommendations: Install an anode-cathode differential pressure transmitter with alarm and a SIL 1 trip

deviation: More Temperature | MCFC stack
causes: Too little reforming heat sink (low feed with high H2 BOG share), excessive current draw, or low cathode air flow
consequences: Stack temperature goes above the design value of about 650 °C. Carbonate evaporates and corrodes the components, seals and separator plates degrade, and gas can leak with a fire risk. Stack life is much reduced.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210, TI-200/TI-210 and TT-410 stack temperature; TE-300 / TI-300 and TE-310 / TI-310 outlet temperatures; BPCS temperature control via SIC-400
recommendations: Add an independent high-high stack temperature trip (SIL 1) that reduces load and fuel; Add high temperature alarms on TI-300/TI-310

deviation: Less Temperature | MCFC stack
causes: Excess air (LCV-200 open), excess feed reforming, prolonged low load, or an uncontrolled cool-down after a trip
consequences: The carbonate electrolyte solidifies (below about 490 °C). The electrolyte matrix cracks and gas crosses over on reheating. The stack is damaged permanently.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring; BPCS temperature control via SIC-400
recommendations: Add a low stack temperature alarm and a procedure for controlled hot standby / heat-up; Consider stack electric heaters for hot standby

deviation: More Power | DC output
causes: Propulsion load demand above stack capability, power converter fault or short circuit
consequences: Current is too high for the fuel supplied, so fuel utilisation is excessive. The anode is starved, cells reverse and overheat, and the stack is damaged. A short circuit can cause arc flash and electrical fire.
safeguards: IE-300 / II-300 / IR-300 current measurement and recording; IT-400 to SIC-400 current control; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm
recommendations: Provide current limiting in the power converter, linked to available fuel flow; Provide DC overcurrent / short-circuit protection on the DC-Power output

deviation: No Power | DC output
causes: DC breaker trip or load rejection by the propulsion system
consequences: The cells reach open-circuit voltage and the voltage goes high. Fuel is not consumed and flows to Anode Out, and the stack cools. The ship loses propulsion power, which in confined waters can lead to collision or grounding.
safeguards: VZA-110 high cell voltage alarm; IE-300 / II-300 current indication; Multiple stack modules providing partial redundancy
recommendations: Implement automatic fuel cutback on load rejection; Review propulsion redundancy and emergency power against class rules

deviation: Reverse Flow | Vent line into stack
causes: BV-160 opens on shutdown or utility failure while stack pressure is low, letting air back in from Vent Out
consequences: Air enters the anode side. A flammable H2/air mixture forms at high temperature and can explode inside the stack. The Ni anode oxidises.
safeguards: BPCS shutdown sequence
recommendations: Provide an inert gas (N2) purge of the anode on shutdown; Install a check valve or flame arrester on the vent line

deviation: No Utility | Instrument air / control power
causes: Loss of instrument air or control power
consequences: BV-400 and BV-410 fail closed and BV-160 fails open. Stack gas, including H2 and CO, is dumped to Vent Out. If the LCVs do not fail closed, fuel keeps flowing to the vent and a flammable cloud forms at the vent outlet. The stack also cools in an uncontrolled way.
safeguards: BV-160 (fail-open) vent valve; PSV-160
recommendations: Confirm that LCV-100 and LCV-300 fail closed, and confirm the LCV-200 fail position; Locate Vent Out in a safe area, backed by hazardous area classification and a dispersion study; Provide a UPS for the control system

deviation: Other than Operation | Stack start-up
causes: H2 BOG or feed is admitted before the stack is purged or brought up to temperature, or the start-up sequence is done in the wrong order
consequences: A flammable mixture forms in the stack and ducts and can explode. Thermal shock and gas crossover follow if the electrolyte is not yet molten. Multiple fatalities are possible in an enclosed machinery space.
safeguards: BPCS start-up sequence; TE-200/TE-210 stack temperature indication
recommendations: Implement start-up permissives (purge complete, stack temperature above electrolyte melting point) before LCV-100/LCV-300 can open; Provide written start-up/shutdown procedures and operator training

deviation: Part of Composition | Stack containment (external leak)
causes: Seal, gasket or flange failure at the stack or its inlet/outlet piping from thermal cycling, ship motion or corrosion
consequences: Hot H2/CO-rich gas is released into the machinery space, with jet fire or explosion and CO poisoning of crew. Multiple fatalities are possible.
recommendations: Install H2 and CO gas detection in the stack enclosure with an ESD (SIL 2) that closes LCV-100/200/300; Provide a ventilated stack enclosure per the IGF Code; Set up an inspection programme for seals and flanges

deviation: Less Level | Electrolyte in stack
causes: Carbonate is gradually lost through evaporation, corrosion and creep over the operating life
consequences: The electrolyte matrix dries out and gas crosses over. Cell voltage falls and local combustion hot spots develop.
safeguards: VE-100 / VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; TE-200/TE-210 temperature monitoring
recommendations: Trend cell voltage deviation for predictive stack replacement

deviation: Reverse Flow | Vent Out / Cathode Out into stack (correction to row 16)
causes: BV-160 opens (fail-open on utility loss or shutdown) or BV-410 is open while stack pressure decays after a trip, so air or exhaust flows back from Vent Out / Cathode Out into the cathode outlet line
consequences: Air enters the cathode outlet line, which also carries anode exhaust routed internally from the anode to the cathode. Air can then migrate through the internal anode-to-cathode path into the anode while residual H2/CO is still present. A flammable mixture can form at about 650 °C, with internal deflagration and stack damage, and the Ni anode oxidises. (Row 16 wrongly says air enters the anode directly.)
safeguards: BPCS shutdown sequence; BV-400 / BV-410 fail-closed on utility loss
recommendations: Provide an inert gas (N2) purge of the anode and cathode on shutdown, before BV-160 vents to atmosphere; Install a check valve or flame arrester on the Vent Out line downstream of BV-160 / PSV-160; Review the shutdown sequence so the stack is not left open to Vent Out / Cathode Out while unpurged

deviation: Less Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
causes: LCV-100 partly closed or a SIC-400 control fault, natural gas compressor degradation, or water pump underperformance
consequences: There is too little fuel for the current drawn, so fuel utilisation is high. The anode is starved locally, cells drop in voltage and can reverse, and the Ni anode oxidises. With less endothermic reforming, the stack temperature rises. Stack life is shortened and power output falls.
safeguards: FIT-100 / FI-100 feed flow indication; PIT-100 / PI-100 feed pressure indication; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; TT-410 / SIC-400 temperature and current control
recommendations: Add a low feed flow alarm on FIT-100 with automatic current limiting through SIC-400 / IT-400

deviation: Less Flow | H2 BOG to anode
causes: LCV-300 partly closed, H2 BOG compressor degradation, or low boil-off from the cargo tanks
consequences: Total fuel to the anode drops. If the feed does not compensate, the anode is starved locally, voltage falls and power falls. The stack is not damaged if the load is reduced.
safeguards: FIT-120 / FI-120 H2 flow indication; PIT-120 / PI-120 H2 pressure indication; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; SIC-400 fuel flow control
recommendations: Add a low H2 flow alarm on FIT-120 with feed-forward compensation through LCV-100

deviation: More Temperature | Feed / air / H2 BOG inlet
causes: Upstream heat exchanger bypass or control failure (outside this node) gives hot inlet gas
consequences: The stack inlet is overheated and thermal gradients form. Carbon can deposit at the reformer inlet from cracking of natural gas. Stack temperature rises and the stack ages faster.
safeguards: TE-100 / TI-100, TE-110 / TI-110 and TE-120 / TI-120 inlet temperature indication; TE-200/TE-210 and TT-410 stack temperature monitoring
recommendations: Add high temperature alarms on TI-100, TI-110 and TI-120

deviation: Less Pressure | Stack anode / cathode
causes: PSV-160 lifts or passes, BV-160 opens spuriously (fail-open), or an external leak occurs
consequences: The stack depressurises and stack gas, including H2 and CO, is released to Vent Out. The anode-cathode differential is upset and gas crosses over. Flammable or toxic gas is released at the vent outlet.
safeguards: PIT-100 / PIT-110 / PIT-120 inlet pressure indication; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm
recommendations: Add position feedback on BV-160 with an alarm; Locate Vent Out in a safe area, confirmed by a dispersion study

deviation: Less Power | DC output
causes: Cell degradation, fuel or air shortfall, or loss of one or more stack modules
consequences: Propulsion power is reduced. Manoeuvrability is limited in confined waters.
safeguards: VE-100 / VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; IE-300 / II-300 / IR-300 current monitoring; Multiple stack modules
recommendations: Provide power management that sheds non-essential load and alarms on the bridge

deviation: As well as Composition | Air to cathode (sea salt / water spray)
causes: Air intake filtration fails or green water / sea spray is drawn into the air compressor intake in heavy weather
consequences: Chlorides and sodium enter the cathode. The cathode and separator plates corrode faster and the carbonate electrolyte is contaminated. Cell performance drops and stack life is shortened (economic loss).
safeguards: VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; TE-110 / TI-110 and PIT-110 / PI-110 air inlet indication
recommendations: Provide marine-grade air intake filtration (salt/coalescing filters) with differential pressure alarm; Locate the air intake away from spray zones and exhaust/vent outlets
